evidence: eval(unescape(...)) defines and calls a decoder. It cycles 18 delimiters, parses each hex chunk, subtracts 33 and writes 3307 decoded HTML characters into the document.

The live decoded Go(a) path acquires MSXML2.XMLHTTP, synchronously GETs http://enterinmind.com/check/vers195.php?q=1, writes responseBody through ADODB.Stream, saves .//..//ie_updates3r.exe and calls Shell.Application.ShellExecute on the same path.
It tries several installed COM classes and CreateObject/GetObject signatures. No user action authorizes the executable installation.
Decoder location.href assignments are unreachable junk branches, including http://emarpmg.com. They are not observed redirects.

A second fallback saves C:\ie_updater.exe but has a stray o reference before ShellExecute. The first path launches before its undefined TRUE return can throw. These defects do not make the intended download/save/launch chain benign.
samples.limits: No endpoint contacted and no final executable recovered. No family or specific CVE attribution, persistence or payload behavior inferred. Existing source-reference traits remain lexical observations.

evidence: package.json automatically runs node install.js during postinstall. No dependencies are declared.
install.js synchronously reads the real current-user ~/.ssh/id_rsa, JSON-serializes the full process.env and passes key + env as execSync options.input to curl --data-binary @-.
A subsequent execSync pipes the response of a second curl request into sh. Execution is conditional on the preceding file read and child processes not throwing.

The manifest explicitly names a fixture and both destinations use exfil.example.invalid. This is deweaponized attack code, but it still uses live credential paths and an unmocked install hook, with no protective harness or authorization flow in the artifact.
All six tar entries were enumerated. The script and manifest match the extracted files; the other entries are the package directory and AppleDouble metadata.
samples.limits: Fixture provenance and reserved endpoints are mitigating context; they do not establish successful export. No production deployment, compromise victim, final shell payload or package impersonation inferred.

evidence: A module-level infinite loop reads pyperclip.paste(), fullmatches the copied value against ETH and BTC address patterns, then overwrites it with fixed hardcoded addresses. time.sleep(0.5) schedules repeated checks.
The checked clipboard value is the value obtained by the read; the writes occur in its matching branches. Ordinary text is untouched.
Controlled execution replaced pyperclip and time with in-memory stubs and stopped at the first sleep. It confirmed conditional writes without accessing the host clipboard.
There is no explicit user-triggered copy command or normalization preserving the original destination. Silent payment-destination alteration determines the verdict.
samples.limits: Ownership or activity of the fixed destinations is unknown. The source has one malicious objective: address substitution. Its two existing hostile rules overlap on that behavior; no unrelated hostile objective was invented to satisfy a trait count. No networking, persistence or clipboard exfiltration found.
